key_insight: A solver-agnostic PINN can train turbulence closures directly from the RANS residual, producing generalizable models across bluff-body shapes without embedding a CFD solver in the optimization loop.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast screening and deployment of turbulence closures that are more portable across geometries, with promising accuracy for mean flow and drag prediction.
method: Train closure forms inside a physics-informed neural network using automatic differentiation to enforce the RANS residual.
Compare four closures: three Reynolds-stress models with realizability constraints and one direct Reynolds-force model without those constraints.
Add input-gradient smoothing and a Lipschitz constraint to improve stability before freezing the learned closure in a finite-element solver.
evidence_signal: The models were trained on six 2D bluff-body wakes at Re = 10^4 and tested with strict leave-one-shape-out evaluation; the force model achieved the best out-of-sample performance, including about 8.5% drag error.
watch_item: Generalization and stability still depend on the downstream solver and the chosen regularization, so frozen deployment should be validated carefully on new geometries and flow regimes.
paper_title: Generalizable turbulence closures across bluff-body shapes by PINN-based solver-agnostic training
